scope: All 24 slides and hover copy reviewed for unfinished verification notes and editorial patterns. Targeted primary-source factual checks, not an independent transaction-level audit of every historic number.

plugin.name: Avoid AI Writing
plugin.mode: extracted prose review; content patches applied to HTML and exports

critical_findings.finding: Nullmask reports service fees and ZEC token rewards separately. Its revenue total adds protocol fees and developer-wallet holder rewards. No automatic service-fee payout is established by these disclosures.
critical_findings.verification_limit: Verified published accounting definitions. Dune query results were not exposed in the retrieved page; Etherscan source access returned 403. No cross-chain fee-to-reward transaction trace is claimed.

critical_findings.finding: Ethereum pool supports ETH/USDT; Base pool supports ETH/USDC. Wallet compatibility is not a partnership, and the operator can read private account history.
The 100K+ wallet figure belongs to retired Aztec Connect. It is not current-network MAU. The comparison now labels the historical product explicitly.
Aztec disclosed the V5 proving vulnerability on 7 August 2026; V6 remediation was planned. The catalyst no longer states a future fix as delivered.
Venice explicitly directs $5 per $100 of purchased API credits to VVV buy-and-burn and documents the 2M annual emission step from 1 October 2026. Existing deck mechanism retained.
Umbra fee-collection documentation routes protocol fees to the governance-set treasury payout account. Existing treasury-versus-holder distinction retained.
Time Tells All reports 95.33% Ethereum mainnet, 96.80% Ethereum testnet, 97.70% Bitcoin testnet and 96.58% Solana testnet under its controlled observer setup. UR was not tested.

Zashi iOS 2.4.7 (5 November 2025) includes ephemeral-address recovery; 2.4.8 (17 November 2025) updates NEAR swaps to unified addresses. The diagram now illustrates address-reuse risk rather than asserting a current implementation defect.
UR price.yml sets initial alpha_per_gib and alpha_per_user to zero. README states market purchases for deposits are expected off-chain, not enforced. Existing conditional deposit wording retained.
Slide 17 remains a clearly marked illustrative chart at the user’s earlier explicit request. No observed monthly series is inferred from the team-reported 350K endpoint.

changes.old: Markets reward privacy only where demand reaches the token
changes.new: Privacy tokens use different routes to value capture
changes.why: Remove an unsupported universal claim about market pricing.

changes.old: Corporate payment flows now settle on public ledgers, and the founders of the industry are building confidentiality into its base layer.
changes.new: Corporate payments are moving onto public ledgers. Buterin and Durov argue for privacy in the networks people already use.
changes.why: Replace broad industry framing with named subjects and a direct claim.

changes.old: Once an address is linked to a company, its payroll, supplier terms and treasury positions become public record.
changes.new: Public payments can reveal a company’s counterparties, payment amounts and treasury balances.
changes.why: Public transactions do not disclose all contractual supplier terms.

changes.old: Tether and Circle issue 84% of supply, so most activity runs through two contracts any analyst can monitor.
changes.new: Tether and Circle account for 84% of supply; their public transfers can be monitored.
changes.why: Supply share does not prove activity share, and these issuers deploy contracts on several chains.

changes.old: At this scale, confidentiality becomes an operating requirement for corporate treasuries rather than a user preference.
changes.new: Public payroll and supplier payments can expose information companies normally keep confidential.
changes.why: Replace a rhetorical contrast with the concrete confidentiality problem.

changes.old: Both positions point to privacy embedded at the infrastructure layer from the outset, which favours protocols over standalone privacy applications.
changes.new: Both argue for privacy in systems people already use. Wallet and application adoption will determine how widely it reaches users.
changes.why: The quoted positions do not establish that protocol tokens outperform applications.

changes.old: Grass and Helium make the same point for network capacity: paying customers and token-level value capture support materially higher valuations.
changes.new: Grass and Helium provide market-cap benchmarks for networks that sell capacity. Their valuations do not establish a fair value for UR (SN25).
changes.why: Keep the comparison without asserting a proven cause of valuation differences.

changes.old: Privacy token landscape
changes.new: Privacy token comparison
changes.why: Use a concrete description of the slide.

changes.old: Private transfers and swaps through existing wallets. Pool entry and exit stay public.
changes.new: Private transfers and swaps. Deposits and withdrawals are public.
changes.why: Explain the public boundaries in plain language.

changes.old: Ethereum and Base documented; MAU not verified
changes.new: Ethereum and Base; supported assets only
changes.why: Report confirmed product availability instead of an unfinished user-count check.

changes.old: Official network documentation lists Ethereum and Base. No independently verified monthly-active-user count is used. Documentation checked 19 October 2026.
changes.new: Official documentation lists ETH and USDT on Ethereum, and ETH and USDC on Base. This cell describes product availability, not a monthly user count. Checked 20 October 2026.
changes.why: State exactly what the source establishes.

changes.old: legacy Connect wallets; current Aztec unverified
changes.new: legacy Connect wallets; retired product
changes.why: The 100K+ figure belongs to the retired Aztec Connect product, not the current network.

changes.old: 100K+ wallets on Aztec Connect, its retired predecessor
changes.new: Aztec reports over 100,000 active wallets for the retired Aztec Connect product. This historical count is not current-network adoption.
changes.why: Make the historical scope explicit.

changes.old: Rewards + burns
changes.new: Reported rewards
changes.why: Avoid presenting reported token metrics as proven product-fee distribution.

changes.old: Analytics reports MASK burns and ZEC payouts. Fee-to-token routing needs verification.
changes.new: Dashboard lists MASK burns and ZEC rewards separately from service fees.
changes.why: Replace the research to-do with the disclosed accounting distinction.

changes.old: MASK is the Solana token. Analytics reports burns and ZEC holder rewards, but this review has not independently traced product-fee-funded buybacks or established a contractual fee entitlement.
changes.new: The pool contract collects product fees. The dashboard adds those fees to developer-wallet ZEC rewards in its revenue total; MASK holder rewards and burns are separate metrics. These disclosures do not establish an automatic product-fee payout to holders.
changes.why: Describe the actual disclosures without claiming a traced cross-chain distribution.

changes.old: Investors are paying for optionality on private use that has yet to materialise at scale.
changes.new: The valuation assumes wider private use than the current activity demonstrates.
changes.why: Replace finance shorthand with the existing argument in plain language.

changes.old: Users keep their wallet setup while shielding activity. The investment case depends on repeat fee-paying usage and a verified path from fees to MASK.
changes.new: Users keep their wallets. Private transfers hide activity from public observers; the operator can read it. MASK rewards are reported separately from service fees.
changes.why: Remove the unresolved verification condition and state the privacy and accounting findings.

changes.old: Existing-wallet access, with visible pool boundaries
changes.new: Deposits and withdrawals remain public
changes.why: Use familiar terms instead of pool-boundary shorthand.

changes.old: How value reaches MASK
changes.new: MASK rewards and burns
changes.why: The evidence supports reported token metrics, not automatic service-fee sharing.

changes.old: Analytics tracks MASK burns and ZEC holder payouts. The share of product fees reaching holders needs on-chain verification.
changes.new: The dashboard reports ZEC holder payouts and MASK burns. It does not document automatic sharing of product fees.
changes.why: State the limit of the published mechanism as a finding rather than a research task.

changes.old: Users pay 0.5% on entry and exit. Reported revenue also includes team-wallet ZEC rewards, so product fees must be assessed separately.
changes.new: Nullmask charges 0.5% on deposits and withdrawals. Its revenue total also includes ZEC rewards paid to the developer wallet.
changes.why: Report the fee and revenue definitions directly.

changes.old: Fee-paying usage repeats as integrations expand. Solana and private perpetuals remain roadmap items; operator visibility is a trust assumption.
changes.new: Repeat paying usage supports the product. Solana and private perpetuals are roadmap targets; the operator can read private activity.
changes.why: Make delivery status and operator visibility explicit.

changes.old: Usage remains small relative to staking and valuation. The chart compares USD amounts on a logarithmic scale. The supplied release disclosures include a critical vulnerability.
changes.new: Aztec disclosed a critical proving bug on 7 August. The chart compares staking, valuation and user funds in USD on a logarithmic scale.
changes.why: Replace editorial scaffolding with the dated primary-source disclosure.

changes.new: Swap boundaries: reused refund addresses can link activity

changes.old: Illustrative only: above the dotted line, assumed deposits exceed miner emissions. No deposit-rate calibration is supplied.
